minutes.headline: Select Board accepted Butterfly Lane as a public way and ratified videographer and assessing appointments.
minutes.summary: The board heard a resident request for remote participation by board members, held two licensing hearings, and heard the library about moving trust funds into higher-return investments. It ratified several town manager appointments, accepted Butterfly Lane, and reviewed Town Meeting warrant articles without making recommendations. A member asked for an executive session on teacher union negotiations.

what_happened.line: The Select Board moved to accept Butterfly Lane as a public way for nominal consideration; the vote result was not audible in the recording.
The board moved to ratify town manager appointments, including videographers as employees and a temporary assessing assistant; results were not audible.
A library trustee described a warrant article letting trustees invest library trust funds under prudent investor rules instead of the town stabilization fund.
The board will wait until March 17 to vote on warrant article recommendations so a full board is present.
After a resident asked for remote participation, staff were to look into video options; a member also requested an executive session on teacher union negotiations.

why_it_matters: Warrant article recommendations, including the library trust fund investment change, go to Town Meeting, where residents vote on them.
The DPW roof low bid exceeded the capital plan amount, and the balance is to come from the facilities budget and unused engineering services funds, so the project touches town spending.
watch_next: March 17 Select Board meeting, when warrant article recommendations are scheduled for a vote.
An executive session to be scheduled before next week's meeting, around 6:30.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main agenda items and most figures. Ours lacks vote results, which the official minutes give, and the captions garble several names and figures. The main gaps are the March 17 warrant-article deferral, which the official minutes omit, and the unclear source and form of the roof funding.
